1.title: Cluster Lifecycle with kubeadm, etcd and High Availability
1.text: Welcome to Module three: Cluster Lifecycle with kube A D M, E T C D and High Availability. It covers the exam area Cluster Architecture, Installation and Configuration. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, and every task was run on a real cluster, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. Prepare underlying infrastructure for installing a Kubernetes cluster. Create and manage Kubernetes clusters using kube A D M. Manage the lifecycle of Kubernetes clusters. Implement and configure a highly-available control plane. Practice with eight hands-on labs worth forty-three points.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Cluster Architecture, Installation and Configuration (twenty-five percent). Practice in this module: eight labs, forty-three points, about forty-three minutes. Exam format: performance-based tasks in a live terminal, scored on the final cluster state. Validated on: Kubernetes version one point thirty-seven point zero.

1.title: What Was Executed and What Is Reference Only
1.text: What Was Executed and What Is Reference Only. The lab cluster is made of containers (kind). Backup and restore of E T C D, certificates, join tokens and draining were executed. kube A D M init, kube A D M join on a new machine, kube A D M upgrade and building a multi-control-plane cluster need separate machines; those parts are marked Reference only (official procedure, not executed here). Practice them in the killer dot S H simulator that comes with the exam.

1.title: Prepare the infrastructure (Reference only, plus two checks you can run)
1.text: Prepare the infrastructure (Reference only, plus two checks you can run). Before kube A D M init every node needs. Swap off. Why: the kubelet does not run with swap on by default. Command: swapoff dash a (and remove it from slash E T C slash fstab ). Packet forwarding. Why: Pods route traffic through the node. Command: sys control net dot ipv four dot ip forward must be one. Bridge traffic seen by I P tables. Why: Service rules apply to bridged traffic. Command: modules overlay and br netfilter, sys control net dot bridge dot bridge nf call I P tables one.

1.title: Prepare the infrastructure (Reference only, plus two checks you can run), continued
1.text: Prepare the infrastructure (Reference only, plus two checks you can run). A container runtime. Why: runs the containers. Command: container D, with Systemd Cgroup true. Matching C group driver. Why: kubelet and runtime must agree. Command: kubelet cgroup Driver systemd in slash var slash lib slash kubelet slash config dot yaml. kube A D M, kubelet, kube control installed and held at one version. Why: the three must be compatible. Command: package manager, then apt mark hold. Open ports. Why: A P I server sixty-four forty-three, E T C D twenty-three seventy-nine-twenty-three eighty, kubelet ten thousand two hundred fifty. Command: firewall or security group. You can check two of these on a node (Lab three point seven). On the test nodes net dot ipv four dot ip forward is one and the kubelet cgroup Driver is systemd.

1.title: Create a cluster with kubeadm (Reference only)
1.text: Create a cluster with kube A D M (Reference only). On the first control plane node. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Create a cluster with kubeadm (Reference only), continued
1.text: Create a cluster with kube A D M (Reference only). kube A D M init creates certificates in slash E T C slash Kubernetes slash pki, kube configs, static Pod manifests, and a bootstrap token. A token lasts twenty-four hours by default; make a new one with kube A D M token create the print join command flag (executed in Lab three point four). kube A D M token list shows them. Without a C N I (Container Network Interface) plugin the nodes stay Not Ready and Core D N S stays Pending.

1.title: etcd backup and restore (executed)
1.text: E T C D backup and restore (executed). The figure shows this: E T C D backup and restore. Exam tip: E T C D C T L snapshot save needs the endpoint and three certificate paths: copy them from the E T C D manifest.

1.title: etcd backup and restore (executed), continued
1.text: E T C D backup and restore (executed). E T C D holds all cluster state. A snapshot is the backup. Find the connection details in the E T C D static Pod manifest ( slash E T C slash Kubernetes slash manifests slash E T C D dot yaml ): the listen address and the three certificate files. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study. Exam tip: After a restore into a new directory, change the host path in the E T C D manifest and restart the control plane Pods.

1.title: etcd backup and restore (executed), continued
1.text: E T C D backup and restore (executed). Restore into a new data directory, then point the E T C D Pod at it. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: etcd backup and restore (executed), continued
1.text: E T C D backup and restore (executed). The kubelet restarts the E T C D Pod when the manifest changes. Finding from the lab, important: after a restore, the A P I server, controller manager and scheduler still hold caches from before the restore. In the test cluster the namespace controller stopped working (namespaces stuck in Terminating, log lines "is not as new as written version") until those three components were restarted. Restart them (move their manifests out of slash E T C slash Kubernetes slash manifests, wait, move them back) and wait for the cluster to answer. Notes for the exam. E T C D C T L is installed on the exam hosts, and E T C D U T L may be needed for restore. On recent versions, E T C D U T L snapshot restore works on the file directly (no endpoints, no certificates).

1.title: etcd backup and restore (executed), continued
1.text: E T C D backup and restore (executed). Do the work on the control plane node named in the task ( S S H node ). Always verify the backup file with snapshot status before declaring it done.

1.title: Certificates
1.text: Certificates. kube A D M leaf certificates are valid for one year by default (the test cluster shows three hundred sixty-four days left after one day); the C A certificates are valid for ten years according to the kube A D M documentation. Check them. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study. Exam tip: kube A D M certs check expiration shows the expiry dates and kube A D M certs renew renews them.

1.title: Certificates, continued
1.text: Certificates. Renew with kube A D M certs renew all (then restart the control plane Pods). Upgrading the cluster with kube A D M upgrade also renews certificates.

1.title: Lifecycle: upgrade (Reference only) and node maintenance (executed)
1.text: Lifecycle: upgrade (Reference only) and node maintenance (executed). The figure shows this: Cluster upgrade order. Exam tip: Upgrade one minor version at a time, and the control plane before the workers.

1.title: Lifecycle: upgrade (Reference only) and node maintenance (executed), continued
1.text: Lifecycle: upgrade (Reference only) and node maintenance (executed). Upgrade order (one minor version at a time, never skip a minor). Control plane node: upgrade the kube A D M package, kube A D M upgrade plan, kube A D M upgrade apply version one dot X dot Y. Drain the node, upgrade kubelet and kube control, restart the kubelet, uncordon. Each other control plane node: kube A D M upgrade node. Each worker: drain, upgrade the kube A D M package, kube A D M upgrade node, upgrade kubelet, restart, uncordon. Node maintenance (Lab three point five).

1.title: Lifecycle: upgrade (Reference only) and node maintenance (executed), continued
1.text: Lifecycle: upgrade (Reference only) and node maintenance (executed). kube control cordon node. marks it unschedulable; running Pods stay. kube control drain node the ignore daemonsets flag. cordons and evicts the Pods (Daemon Set Pods are skipped); needed for any node with workloads. kube control uncordon node. makes it schedulable again. drain refuses to evict Pods that use local storage ( empty dir ) or are not managed by a controller unless you add the delete emptydir data flag or the force flag. Pods that belong to a Deployment are recreated on other nodes.

1.title: High availability (concept; Reference only)
1.text: High availability (concept; Reference only). Stacked E T C D. E T C D location: E T C D runs on each control plane node. Trade-off: simpler; losing a node loses a control plane member and an E T C D member. External E T C D. E T C D location: separate E T C D nodes. Trade-off: more machines; control plane and E T C D fail independently. Use an odd number of E T C D members (three or five). A quorum (majority) must be up: three members tolerate one failure, five tolerate two. Put a load balancer in front of the A P I servers; kube A D M init the control plane endpoint flag set to lb sixty-four forty-three the upload certs flag and kube A D M join... the control plane flag add more control plane nodes. Scheduler and controller manager use leader election: only one is active at a time. Workers need no change; they reach the A P I through the load balancer.

1.title: Lab 3.1: etcd backup
1.text: Lab three point one: E T C D backup. This task is worth seven points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. On the control plane node C K A control plane, take a snapshot of E T C D and save it as slash opt slash backup slash E T C D dot db. Find the endpoint and the certificate paths in the E T C D static Pod manifest. E T C D C T L is installed on the node. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

1.title: Lab 3.1: etcd backup, Solution
1.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run S S H C K A control plane grep dash E cert file key file trusted ca file listen client slash E T C slash Kubernetes slash manifests slash E T C D dot, and so on. Then S S H C K A control plane E T C D C T L the endpoints flag set to H T T P S colon slash slash one hundred twenty-seven dot zero dot, and so on. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

1.title: Lab 3.2: etcd restore
1.text: Lab three point two: E T C D restore. This task is worth eight points, and you should plan about ten minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. A snapshot of E T C D exists at slash opt slash backup slash E T C D before dot db on C K A control plane. The namespace keep was deleted by mistake after that snapshot. Restore the cluster from the snapshot so that namespace keep exists again. Use the new data directory slash var slash lib slash E T C D restore and make the E T C D static Pod use it. The cluster must be healthy at the end: restart the control plane components that cache cluster state so that they pick up the restored data. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 3.2: etcd restore, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run S S H C K A control plane E T C D U T L snapshot restore slash opt slash backup slash E T C D before dot db the data dir flag slash, and so on. Then S S H C K A control plane sed dash i s path slash var slash lib slash E T C D path slash var slash lib slash E T C D restore slash, and so on. Then S S H C K A control plane mkdir dash p slash tmp slash off mv slash E T C slash Kubernetes slash manifests slash kube- A P I server,controller manager,scheduler dot yaml slash, and so on. Then until kube control get the raw flag slash readyz slash dev slash null two one do sleep two done. Then kube control wait the for flag set to condition Ready node the all flag the timeout flag set to one hundred eighty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 3.3: cert expiry
2.text: Lab three point three: cert expiry. This task is worth four points, and you should plan about four minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. On the control plane node, find the date on which the certificate of the A P I server ( slash E T C slash Kubernetes slash pki slash A P I server dot crt ) expires. Write it exactly as Open S S L prints the not After value (for example Nov nine eighteen thirty-nine one two thousand twenty-seven G M T ) to about slash answers slash expiry dot txt on the host. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 3.3: cert expiry, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run S S H C K A control plane kube A D M certs check expiration two slash dev slash null grep dash E ^A P I server. Then S S H C K A control plane open S S L X five oh nine -in slash E T C slash Kubernetes slash pki slash A P I server dot crt -noout -enddate, and so on. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 3.4: join command
2.text: Lab three point four: join command. This task is worth five points, and you should plan about four minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. A new worker node must join the cluster. On the control plane node, create a new bootstrap token and save the complete kube A D M join command (with token and C A certificate hash) to about slash answers slash join dot txt on the host. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 3.4: join command, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run S S H C K A control plane kube A D M token create the print join command flag two slash dev slash null about slash answers slash join dot txt. Then cat about slash answers slash join dot txt. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 3.5: drain node
2.text: Lab three point five: drain node. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. Node C K A worker two needs maintenance. Make it unschedulable and evict the workloads from it, leaving the Daemon Set Pods alone (Pods that use empty dir volumes may be deleted). A Deployment web in the namespace maint (four replicas) must still have all four replicas Ready afterwards, on the other nodes. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 3.5: drain node, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control drain C K A worker two the ignore daemonsets flag the delete emptydir data flag. Then kube control dash n maint rollout status deployment web the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 3.6: etcd members
2.text: Lab three point six: E T C D members. This task is worth four points, and you should plan about four minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. Using E T C D C T L on the control plane node, find the name of the E T C D member (as shown by the member list) and write it to about slash answers slash member dot txt on the host. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 3.6: etcd members, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run S S H C K A control plane E T C D C T L the endpoints flag set to H T T P S colon slash slash one hundred twenty-seven dot zero dot, and so on. Then S S H C K A control plane E T C D C T L the endpoints flag set to H T T P S colon slash slash one hundred twenty-seven dot zero dot, and so on. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 3.7: node prereqs
2.text: Lab three point seven: node prereqs. This task is worth four points, and you should plan about four minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. Before installing Kubernetes on a node you check two prerequisites on C K A worker. Write to about slash answers slash prereq dot txt two lines: line one is the value of the kernel setting net dot ipv four dot ip forward (zero or one), line two is the C group driver the kubelet is configured with (the cgroup Driver value in the kubelet configuration file). Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 3.7: node prereqs, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run S S H C K A worker sys control dash n net dot ipv four dot ip forward about slash answers slash prereq dot txt. Then S S H C K A worker grep cgroup Driver slash var slash lib slash kubelet slash config dot yaml awk print two about slash answers slash prereq dot txt. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 3.8: kubeadm config
2.text: Lab three point eight: kube A D M config. This task is worth five points, and you should plan about five minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. kube A D M stores the cluster configuration in a Config Map. Find the kubernetes Version and the cluster Name recorded in the Cluster Configuration and write them to about slash answers slash kube A D M dot txt on the host, two lines: kubernetes Version value then cluster Name value. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 3.8: kubeadm config, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n kube system get configmap kube A D M config dash o json path dot data dot Cluster Configuration grep dash E ^ kubernetes Version cluster Name sort dash r about, and so on. Then cat about slash answers slash kube A D M dot txt. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Recall Check 1
2.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Which flag of E T C D C T L snapshot save files must you take from the E T C D manifest? Answer: The endpoint and the C A, server certificate and server key paths ( the cacert flag, the cert flag, the key flag ). Question two. After restoring E T C D to a new directory, what must change so the cluster uses it? Answer: The host path of the data volume in the E T C D static Pod manifest. Question three. Why restart the A P I server, controller manager and scheduler after a restore? Answer: They hold caches from before the restore; stale caches break controllers (for example namespaces stay Terminating ).

2.title: Recall Check 2
2.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. How do you get a new kube A D M join command after the first token expired? Answer: kube A D M token create the print join command flag on a control plane node. Question five. What is the difference between cordon and drain? Answer: cordon only stops new scheduling; drain also evicts the existing Pods (use the ignore daemonsets flag ). Question six. Can you upgrade from version one point thirty-five to version one point thirty-seven in one step? Answer: No; upgrade one minor version at a time.

2.title: Recall Check 3
2.text: Recall check three. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question seven. How many E T C D members tolerate one failure, and why odd numbers? Answer: three. A majority (quorum) must stay up; an odd count gives the best fault tolerance for the size. Question eight. Which command lists certificate expiry dates on a kube A D M cluster? Answer: kube A D M certs check expiration.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Prepare nodes: swap off, ip forward equals one, br netfilter, container D with systemd C groups. Init or join: kube A D M init, then C N I, kube A D M token create the print join command flag. E T C D backup: E T C D C T L snapshot save with the endpoints flag the cacert flag the cert flag the key flag; verify with E T C D U T L snapshot status. E T C D restore: E T C D U T L snapshot restore the data dir flag new, edit manifest host path, restart control plane components. Certs: kube A D M certs check expiration, kube A D M certs renew. Maintenance: cordon, drain the ignore daemonsets flag, uncordon. Upgrade: one minor at a time; control plane first; kube A D M upgrade plan slash apply slash node. H A (high availability): odd E T C D count, load balancer, stacked or external E T C D, leader election. In the next module, we continue the course.
